sections.body: Governance, ethics and research integrity is the part of AI research that asks who is accountable for AI assisted work, what counts as evidence, and how data and images can be traced. In practice, AI tools now draft text, suggest citations, screen manuscripts, flag image duplication, and help reviewers check statistical claims. Authorship questions arise when a model contributes to drafting or analysis, because tools cannot take responsibility, consent, or accountability. Fact checking systems compare generated claims against sources, but they often miss fabricated references that look plausible. Training data provenance work traces which papers, books, and datasets were used, and under what terms. Ethics review with AI assistance is being tested for triage and consistency, while humans still make the judgments.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are partly solved. Citation checking can catch references that do not exist when a database is queried, and image forensics can reveal duplication or splicing in some cases. But hallucinated citations remain a serious problem because models generate fluent, plausible references that may mix real authors, real journals, and wrong titles. Provenance is uneven, since many models do not disclose training sources and many publishers do not require data statements. Ethics review with AI assistance is not settled, because reviewers must weigh context, vulnerability, and consent, which are hard to encode. The honest limits are that AI can assist detection and documentation, but it cannot certify integrity, assign responsibility, or replace human judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The page on AI and Authorship examines who can be listed, what contributions mean, and how journals are responding. Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking looks at hallucinated references, verification workflows, and why a generated citation can pass a casual read. Training Data and Academic Work covers the provenance of papers, books, and datasets used in model development, including licensing and consent questions. Ethics Review with AI Assistance describes how review boards and editors are experimenting with AI for screening and consistency, and where human oversight remains necessary. Provenance of Research Images and Data explains how image forensics, metadata, and data statements help trace evidence from collection to publication. A reader can move from authorship rules to verification methods, then to the upstream data and image trails that make research claims checkable, and the library's 135 research papers give a concrete base for tracing how these questions are handled in practice.
